entries.core_move: Convert a sinusoid's amplitude and phase into the fixed $t=0 complex phasor that anchors its later rotation and axis projections$.
Track a phasor as uniform rotation in the complex plane by computing its instantaneous angle from initial phase and angular frequency.
Classify phasor rotation as counterclockwise or clockwise by using the sign of angular frequency to determine the direction of phase progression.
Compute the cosine-valued time signal obtained by projecting a rotating phasor onto the real axis using its magnitude, angular frequency, rotation direction, and initial phase.
Compute the sine-valued time signal obtained by projecting a rotating phasor onto the imaginary axis and interpreting the result as its imaginary component.
Convert $A\cos(\omega t + \phi)$ into $\operatorname{Re}\{Ae^{j\phi}e^{j\omega t}\}$ and its equivalent conjugate complex-exponential sum.
Convert $A\sin(\omega t + \phi)$ into $\frac{A}{2j}e^{j(\omega t+\phi)} - \frac{A}{2j}e^{-j(\omega t+\phi)}$ by interpreting sine as the imaginary-axis projection of a rotating phasor.
Decompose a real sine or cosine into paired complex exponentials at positive and negative angular frequencies and interpret their conjugate coefficients as counter-rotating phasor components.
